title: Image count by class and split
why: A grouped count plot checks coverage and split composition.
insight: Counts are calculated directly from the supplied folders, making class imbalance visible before training.
business_impact: The training plan can use class-aware metrics and class weights if the imbalance affects recall.

title: Overall class percentage
why: Percentages make imbalance easier to compare than raw counts.
insight: Each bar shows the share of all images assigned to a class.
business_impact: Balanced evaluation avoids letting the largest class dominate reported accuracy.

title: Image width distribution
why: A width histogram checks whether resizing is required.
insight: The supplied images share a consistent width, so model resizing is standardization rather than repair for mixed dimensions.
business_impact: A consistent input pipeline reduces preprocessing surprises.

title: Image height distribution
why: A height histogram complements width inspection.
insight: The supplied images share a consistent height.
business_impact: Uniform source dimensions support deterministic batching.

title: Aspect ratio distribution
insight: The images have a 1:1 aspect ratio, so resizing to a square input does not introduce geometric distortion.
business_impact: Preserving shape reduces a preventable source of visual artifacts.

title: Mean brightness distribution
why: Brightness highlights acquisition and preprocessing variability.
insight: The distribution is measured from grayscale pixel values normalized to [0, 1].
business_impact: Contrast-aware augmentation can improve robustness to scanner and protocol differences.

title: Within-image contrast distribution
why: Per-image standard deviation is a simple contrast proxy.
insight: The chart compares grayscale intensity spread across images.
business_impact: Very low contrast samples may need review or careful augmentation.

title: Brightness by class
why: A class box plot checks whether brightness differs systematically by label.
insight: Boxes show the observed distribution for each class, not a causal effect.
business_impact: Systematic acquisition differences could become shortcuts, so results should be validated on external data.

title: Contrast by class
why: A class box plot checks contrast differences across labels.
insight: The observed spread identifies whether some classes are visually easier or harder due to contrast.
business_impact: Model performance should be read alongside per-class recall.

title: Aspect ratio by class
why: A class comparison checks whether geometry is label-dependent.
insight: All folders use the same square source geometry.
business_impact: There is no evidence here that aspect ratio can act as a class shortcut.

title: Representative image per class
why: A labeled gallery validates that folder labels match visible sample content.
insight: The gallery is selected deterministically from each class.
business_impact: Visual inspection is a basic safety check before training a medical-imaging classifier.

title: Randomized image grid
why: A grid exposes variation that a single sample can hide.
insight: The displayed images are sampled with a fixed seed for reproducibility.
business_impact: Variation supports decisions about augmentation and error review.

title: Augmentation examples
why: Before training, transformations should be visually inspected for plausibility.
insight: The panel applies mild flips, rotation, zoom, and contrast changes to a representative image.
business_impact: Plausible augmentation can improve generalization without creating anatomically implausible images.

title: Pixel intensity distributions by class
why: Intensity curves compare the full grayscale value distribution by label.
insight: Curves summarize actual pixels from the dataset rather than model outputs.
business_impact: Strong differences may indicate acquisition bias and motivate external validation.

title: Split composition by class
why: A normalized stacked bar chart checks whether train, valid, and test have similar class proportions.
insight: The provided split proportions can be compared without being confounded by split size.
business_impact: A representative test set makes model comparison more credible.
